deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck sets up a category of decorated surfaces (the objects of SCD / SCD^+ on the next page). Such an object is (X, Σ, R): a compact oriented surface X with boundary ∂X, a closed 1-submanifold Σ of cutting circles in the interior, and a marking or 'ribbon' datum R. The dual combinatorial gadget is a weighted graph, possibly with ribbons or regions. Its vertices are the components of X∖Σ, weighted by genus. Its ordinary edges A_0 = π_0(Σ) are the cutting circles. Its free edges A_ℓ = π_0(∂X) are the boundary circles (holes). He is listing elementary 'erasure' (gommage) operations between such objects and how each is reflected on the graphs. These are the face and degeneracy maps of the stratification of Teichmüller/moduli spaces, i.e. the Teichmüller tower or 'Lego'.

Item 1 (previous page) erases a sub-ribbon structure R' stable under σ0, σ1. Item 2 (previous page) erases a subset Σ' of cutting circles; on graphs this contracts the corresponding ordinary edges, giving a generization morphism.

Item 3 (this page), filling holes (bouchage des trous). Given a closed 1-submanifold of ∂X, equivalently a subset A'_ℓ ⊂ π_0(∂X) ≅ A_ℓ, glue the cone (a disc) onto each of the chosen boundary circles. On the graph this deletes the corresponding free edges together with the 'régions de rognage' lying over them. Vertex weights (genera) are unchanged, which is correct since capping a boundary circle by a disc does not change genus.

Item 4 (this page), mixed simultaneous erasures. Take an open-and-closed subset (a union of components) R'⊔Σ' of R⊔Σ, equivalently R'⊔A' ⊂ R⊔A. Require R' ⊃ R|Σ' (R|A'), so that ribbons sitting on erased circles are erased with them. On weighted graphs with ribbons or regions this removes the corresponding part of R̄ and contracts the edges of A' (and of F'_pos, regarded as free), with weights following as in item 2.

In modern terms this is the composite of a forgetful map and a boundary-stratum generization in a category of stable or ribbon graphs: the structure maps of a modular-operad-like or 'graph category' of decorated surfaces.
errors: Item 3 does not address stability: capping holes can produce unstable pieces (discs, or spheres with fewer than 3 holes or marked points), and no condition is imposed here. This may be handled elsewhere in the notes.

The exact meaning of 'F'_pos' and of the contraction in item 4 is sketchy on the page; it is not fully explicit how the weights add when several edges forming cycles are contracted (genus increases by the first Betti number of the contracted subgraph). Item 2 says this is to be made explicit.

ideas.what: Capping boundary components by cones/discs and the corresponding deletion of free edges (legs) of the dual weighted graph, genus weights unchanged
ideas.modern_name: Capping/forgetful map on boundary components (Harer-type capping maps); deleting legs in stable graphs
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower and its 'Lego' in general terms; no explicit treatment of this operation known

ideas.what: Simultaneous mixed erasure of a clopen set of cutting circles and ribbons, with the compatibility R' ⊃ R|Σ', realized as edge contraction plus ribbon deletion on weighted ribbon graphs
ideas.modern_name: Composite morphisms in the category of stable/ribbon graphs (edge contractions + forgetful maps); structure maps of modular operads; specialization/generization in the stratification of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen, Deligne–Mumford (boundary strata); Kontsevich; Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998)
ideas.where_published: Ideas of the Teichmüller Lego in Esquisse d'un programme; details unpublished

missed.claim: A 1983 systematic catalogue of the elementary morphisms (erase ribbons, contract cutting-circle edges, cap holes, mixed composites) of a category of decorated surfaces and of their dual weighted ribbon graphs. This anticipates the graph categories underlying modular operads and the combinatorial stratification of moduli of curves.
missed.quote: Gommages simultanés mixtes, correspondant à une partie R'⊔Σ' de R⊔Σ qui soit à la fois ouverte et fermée ... telle que R' ⊃ R|A'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest: it documents how concretely Grothendieck had worked out the combinatorics behind the 'Teichmüller Lego' before Getzler–Kapranov and the ribbon-graph literature. The content itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine bookkeeping of operations on surfaces and dual graphs. The constructions are now standard (stable-graph contractions, forgetful/capping maps). Interest is mainly as early unpublished groundwork for the Teichmüller Lego.
transcription_corrections: 'Au niveau des graphes, elle consiste à gommer les arêtes libres correspondantes, ou bien entendu aussi les régions de rognage qui se trouvent au dessus' – the struck word after the dash is 'mais', and the sentence continues 'les pondérations des sommets restant inchangées' (reading looks right).
Item 4: 'à contracter ensuite les arêtes de F'_pos (considérées comme libres par là?)' – 'en un sommet' in the machine transcription is doubtful; the image suggests 'à contracter ensuite'.
Item 3 refers to the components of the boundary of 'Σ'_ℓ' (the chosen part of ∂X), not of Σ.
